articleTitle: Synthesizing Realistic Cracked Terrain for Virtual Arid Environment Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Virtual environments play a pivotal role in various applications such as video games, simulations, and virtual reality experiences. Creating realistic and immersive virtual arid environments necessitates the generation of terrain featuring cracked surfaces, mirroring the parched landscapes of arid regions. This paper presents a novel approach for synthesizing realistic cracked terrain to enhance the authenticity of virtual arid environments. We explore the underlying principles of terrain generation, the significance of realistic cracked features, and the computational techniques used to achieve this realism. Through a series of numerical experiments, we validate the correctness of our proposed technical approach for synthesizing realistic cracked terrain for virtual arid environment generation.

articleTitle: A GAN-Based Channel Estimation Method for MIMO OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Accurate channel estimation is crucial for communication systems. This paper proposes a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) based method which can significantly improve the performance of channel estimation. Specifically, we first train two GANs to learn the receive and transmit correlation information, respectively. Through backpropagation, the parameters in the GANs are continuously updated until the distribution characteristics of the channels are learned. After that, we use these two trained GANs to perform online channel estimation separately. At this stage, GANs will search for latent vectors and complete the channel estimation with a very limited number of pilots. Finally, we linearly combine the outputs of two GANs to obtain the final channel estimates. According to the simulation results, the proposed method outperforms the channel estimation method without utilizing spatial correlation, since it fully utilizes channel correlation information.

articleTitle: Improved ORB-GRAND for PAC Codes
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Polarization-adjusted convolutional (PAC) codes have been proposed to significantly improve error correction ability compared to polar codes by incorporating rate-1 convolutional precoding. However, the development of computationally efficient decoders for PAC codes is still an ongoing research area. Ordered Reliability Bit Guessing Random Additive Noise Decoding (ORB-GRAND), a universal near Maximum Likelihood (near-ML) decoder, has been introduced for decoding moderately redundant block codes by querying a list of putative test error patterns (TEP) in a fixed order, i.e. logistic weight order (LWO) and improved logistic weight order (iLWO). In this study, we undertake a comprehensive investigation into the performance of ORB-GRAND concerning high-rate PAC codes of short-to-medium length. Firstly, we conduct a comparative analysis between ORB-GRAND and successive cancellation list (SCL) decoding for PAC codes and integrate the Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) mechanism into ORB-GRAND. Distance properties of PAC and CRC-Aided PAC (CA-PAC) codes are explored to demonstrate the performance results. Secondly, we propose a novel TEP scheduling scheme in response to the distinctive reduction in BLER revealed by scheduling TEP in iLWO, particularly for short PAC codes under low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) conditions. This remarkable scheme demonstrates its efficacy by effectively mitigating the aforementioned BLER degradation while maintaining the exceptional performance of iLWO in high SNR conditions.

articleTitle: Influence of Co-Frequency Interference on Transmission Performance in Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Frequency and orbital resources become more and more tightly, with the rapid deployment and application of low-orbit satellite systems in the world. The potential threat of cofrequency interference between different satellites, or between the different satellite beams for multiple-beam satellite systems. Because of the clear advantage of the short communication distance between the satellite and ground, the loss of the free space and transmission delay are a lot smaller than geo-stationary orbit (GEO) satellites. The superiority from short distance indicates that the transmitted power from the satellite and user-end could be much smaller than the situation of high-order systems. The power reduction is accompanied with the utilizing of high-order modulation method for improving the utilization efficiency of spectrum with the increasing of communication capacity, which is the development trend of satellite communication in future. The degree of co-frequency interference is crucial to the transmission performance of the system. It can provide some references for the analysis of co-frequency interference in future.

articleTitle: Medical IoT Platform with its Applications in Total Course of Disease and Health Management
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Medical data collected from different healthcare scenarios and a variety of IoT platforms is inevitably fragmented, partial and incomplete. In an effort to mitigate the problem, a single medical IoT platform was utilized to cover both total course of disease and health management. And a set of technique standards were applied for easier connections of diverse medical IoT devices. In addition, the key techniques, architecture and applications of the presented platform across total course of disease and health management were introduced in this paper. So far the presented platform has been commercially employing and showed its potential to health data fusion, analysis and decision making. Furthermore, comprehensive coverage of health data across scenarios and devices is highly beneficial to next-generation of accurate health services, course analysis and medical predictions.

articleTitle: Time Domain Attention Mechanism Based Multi-Functional Radar Working Mode Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: With the rapid development of radar technology, multi-functional radars have been widely used in land, sea, air, and space. Due to the ability of multi-functional radar (MFR) to vary parameters freely with the change in battlefield scene, traditional classification network based radar working mode recognition method can no longer handle well. Therefore, a multi-function radar working mode recognition method using attention mechanism is proposed. Utilizing the Time Domain Attention Mechanism (TDAM) to assign different weights to pulse amplitude and waveform sequences at different times, enhancing the level of attention to key time data. Then, a concatenate convolutional neural network (CNN) is used for feature extraction and classification. In consideration of the receiver sensitivity and reconnaissance duration, simulation results have shown the proposed method is superior to convolutional neural networks (CNN) and convolutional autoencoder (CAE) methods.

articleTitle: Weighted Sum-Rate Maximization for RIS-Assisted MU-MIMO Communication Systems with Low-Resolution ADCs/DACs
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This paper focuses on maximizing the weighted sum-rate (WSR) in downlink communication systems that uti-lize reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) to enhance MU-MIMO transmission. To reduce implementation costs and power consumption, low-resolution ADCs/DACs are configured at the BS. Unlike the traditional design that predicated on perfect channel state information (CSI), we establish a WSR optimization problem given imperfect estimated CSI. Specifically, based on imperfect statistical CSI, we propose a robust weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) algorithm to maximize the beam-forming matrix, and then use riemann conjugate gradient (RCG) algorithm to optimize the phase shift vector with the aim of maximizing the WSR for all users. Numerical examples indicate that the proposed scheme improves system's robustness as well as achieves optimal WSR performance using three quantization bits.

articleTitle: Simulated Annealing Genetic Algorithm based RIS Phase Optimization in the High-Speed Communication of the Railways
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The aim is to solve the problem of unstable and discontinuous signal transmission in the wireless communication of the High-Speed Railway (HSR). In the RIS mobile wireless communication system for highways, the active radiation and the RIS discrete phase at the basis station are jointly optimized in order to maximize the system capacity under the restrictions of the transmitting strength of the basic station and RIS discrete phase shift. Firstly, the closed-form solution of the base station beam allocation is derived using the generalized Rayleigh entropy theorem. Then the Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm was invented as an improvement on the standard Genetic Algorithm (GA). The enhanced genetic algorithm is used to solve discrete phase of RIS. The results of the simulation show that the overall effectiveness of the system with RIS is significantly higher than the system without RIS. The SA-GA, which significantly outperforms standard genetic algorithm and achieves fast convergence.

articleTitle: Poisoning Attack-Based Security Evaluation Framework for Credit Risk Evaluation Models
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Machine learning has been widely used in the field of credit risk evaluation (CRE). However, existing studies have mainly focused on the evaluation performance of the models, and little attention has been paid to the security of machine learning models. It has been shown that machine learning models are susceptible to the influence of adversarial samples and thus make incorrect judgments. In this paper, we propose a security evaluation framework based on poisoning attack for CRE models (SEF-PAC), using Generative Adversarial Nets (GAN) to achieve automatic large batch generation of adversarial samples, and evaluate the security of 8 CRE machine learning models in the face of poisoning attack. It is found that the adversarial samples generated using GAN are still transferable to the 8 CRE machine learning models under poisoning attack, and are able to make target models significantly less accurate in identifying samples with bad credit without a significant decrease in overall classification accuracy. This indicates that the current machine learning-based CRE models have huge security risks and proves the feasibility and effectiveness of the security evaluation framework proposed in this paper, which provides an important reference for enterprises to evaluate and improve the security of CRE models.

articleTitle: A Principal Direction Detection based Porcelain Insulator Location for Transmission Line Infrared Images
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Porcelain insulator is important for the safety of transmission lines, and infrared detection is a key way to find insulators degradation. However, there is a lack of fast insulator location method to automatically identify the deterioration status. In this paper, we propose a method for porcelain insulator location in infrared image based on principal direction detection. Considering the various insulator orientation in the image, we first detect the principal direction of the insulator in the infrared image. Secondly, the orientation is removed from the whole image. By searching the insulator regions along the horizontal direction, the insulator can be located easily. We use 300 infrared images to check the proposed method, the experimental results prove its performance. For infrared images captured for porcelain insulator of a high voltage transmission line, we provide a flexible method to get the steel cap location. With temperature data of located points, the temperature difference could provide quantitative analysis basis for insulator deterioration state diagnosis.

articleTitle: Pixel Transformer for Synthetic-to-Real Single Image Dehazing
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Existing dehazing methods are always unsatisfactory on real images. In this paper, we propose a novel dehazing model Pixel Transformer with an encoder-decoder structure based on the self-attention mechanism. First, a non-homogeneous synthetic haze dataset, NHS-Haze, is constructed using a random sampling stitching method to simulate real images. Second, to capture the similarity of the internal structure of the image, an encoder consisting of two basic blocks accompanied by a patch merging layer is designed. Also, a pixel shuffle layer is added after each basic block in the decoder to reconstruct the details from the feature maps. Third, the NHS-Haze dataset is used to decrease the domain difference between the real and synthetic images to mitigate the domain drift problem. Finally, cross-testing is performed on the public, synthetic dataset Haze4K and SOTA methods to evaluate the robustness of each dehazing model on different datasets under realistic scenarios.

articleTitle: Intrinsic Plasticity Deep Echo State Networks for Industrial Soft Sensor Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In industrial process, the acquisition of crucial quality variables is of great significance for industrial process control. However, due to problems such as harsh environments and equipment failures, obtaining crucial variables in a timely manner poses a significant challenge. In this paper, a soft sensor modeling method based on the intrinsic plasticity deep echo state network(IPDESN) is proposed. A hierarchical dynamic reservoirs structure is used to obtain the high-dimensional feature representation of the inputs, and the intrinsic plasticity (IP) mechanism is used to maximize the information transmitted by the reservoir neurons adaptively. The nonlinear support vector regression(NLSVR) is introduced for output training. The proposed method is applied to estimate the acid gas including hydrogen sulfide(H2S) and sulfur dioxide(SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) concentration in a sulfur processing unit(SRU) to verify its performance. In comparison to other soft sensor methods, the experimental results show that the proposed IPDESN-NLSVR method demonstrates superior performance, achieving significantly higher modeling accuracy in industrial process.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Learning Based on Deep Learning for Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This paper focuses on metric-based few-shot learning, in which the model adjusts its parameters according to the model performance on the meta-tasks encountered during training to obtain a robust model parameter distribution, and the final model performance may lead to overfitting problems due to the small number of samples used to define the categories. Given such problems, a parameter adaptive adjustment mechanism is introduced in the paper to determine the main source of the current model error and to adjust the gradient backpropagation strength in this way to prevent overfitting problems due to sampling errors during the meta-learning training phase. In the paper, a few-shot image classification algorithm based on cross-attention subspace metric is proposed in the framework of existing few-shot image classification algorithms, using a cross-attention mechanism to correlate information between support set sample features and a query set sample features, and then project them into space separately. Different subspaces represent different categories, and the classification accuracy of the model can be improved by measuring the distance between the samples to be measured and the subspaces while increasing the distance between different subspaces to distinguish the samples of different categories. To verify the effectiveness of the method, the proposed method is validated on Mini-ImageNet and tiered-ImageNet, the common datasets for few-shot images, and compared with the classical few-shot image classification algorithm, and the experimental results show that the classification accuracy is improved on both datasets.

articleTitle: Efficient Wi-Fi Device RF Fingerprint Detection and Classification Using Wigner-Ville Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In the realm of Internet of Things (IoT) applications, Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification (RFFI) is emerging as a robust technique for enhancing wireless security based on the inherent hardware attributes in wireless devices. We proposed and demonstrated a robust scheme achieved by the statistical extraction method based on Wigner- Ville Distribution analysis for Wi - Fi devices. The proposed framework attains full authentication using a low-complexity feature extractor and employs K-nearest neighbor algorithm for both detecting rogue devices and classifying legitimate devices. This work shows the suitability of statistical feature extraction for rogue device detection. An excellent recognition accuracy of 97.64 % is experimentally demonstrated, with a false alarm rate of 3.29% and a miss alarm rate of 0%, using 11 wireless network interface controllers. Notably, the computational efficiency of our RFFI scheme, achieved through lightweight and straightforward feature extraction method, positions it as a viable solution for security enhancement in resource-constrained wireless communications.

articleTitle: MPFFNet:Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Image Buildings Based on Multipath Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The buildings with variable scales and complex background information in remote sensing images often result in missed and misclassified segmentation of buildings. To address this issue, this paper designs an multipath feature fusion network (MPFFNet). MPFFNet has an overall encoding and decoding structure, embedded with an residual depth Inception block(RDI) module to extract multi-scale features. At the same time, MPFFNet uses the multipath residual channel attention (MPRCA) module to expand the Receptive field of the feature map to obtain rich multi-scale context information. The validity of the proposed algorithm is proved on the WHU Buildings data set, with F1 reaching 94.70%, IOU reaching 89.93%, and Recall reaching 94.98%.

articleTitle: Cardiac Medical Image Segmentation Based on Parallel Fusion Network Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide. Accurate segmentation of cardiac images is able to assist physicians in quantifying and locating abnormal regions and cells in the heart, facilitating diagnosis and treatment and consequently reducing cardiovascular death rate. Semantic segmentation models have been widely used for this task in recent years. However, the task is challenging due to the complex anatomy of the heart and the presence of noise and variations in grayscale in cardiac medical images, which require high segmentation accuracy. To address this challenge, a feature-enhancement model based on Vision-Transformer-Unet (VIT-Unet) is proposed. Specifically, a parallel network that consists of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Win-Transformer modules with windowed attention is constructed to extract comprehensive features. Then, a Fusion Convolution Transformer is added to enable the integration of global and local features from the parallel network. Finally, the Transformer module in the baseline model is replaced with our parallel fusion feature extraction network. The method proposed in the paper not only achieves higher segmentation accuracy but also presents more robust results compared to the baseline model, as evidenced by the experimental findings.

articleTitle: Research on Vehicle Pricing Factors of Auto Insurance Based on Machine Leaning
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In this paper, the claim data and vehicle configuration data of insurance companies are taken as the research object, and the vehicle pricing factors of auto insurance are screened based on GLM and four machine learning algorithms. By calculating the importance of each factor and sorting it and taking the intersection, the last 14 influence factors were obtained. According to the MSE results, the fitting effect of XGBoost model is superior. The research outcomes and model algorithm will provide an important methodological reference for the selection of auto insurance pricing elements in China, as well as a significant foundation for the personalization of auto insurance.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Imaging Based on Double Spiral Sparse Sampling with Equivalent Arc Length Interval
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: A double spiral sparse sampling method with equivalent arc length interval is presented in this paper for millimeter wave imaging. First, double Archimedes spirals are adopted to form sparse sampling pattern. Next, the positions of the sampling points on the spirals are derived to make the arc length interval of the adjacent sampling points equivalent. Millimeter wave imaging method based on principle of back-projection (BP) is designed for image reconstruction. Experiments with both numerical simulated data and real data have been conducted to compare the reconstruction performances under different sampling patterns. The experimental results have verified the effectiveness of the proposed sparse sampling method.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment for Complex Systems by Fusing Multi-Stage Test Information
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: To solve the problem that the reliability assessment of complex systems was difficult due to the lack of reliability information in the development stage, a hybrid Bayesian assessment method based on KL divergence was proposed in this paper. The probability distribution of the failure rate at each test stage was calculated using reliability test data from the previous development stages, which were transferred as the prior distribution in the final test stage, and then Bayesian theory was used to calculate the posterior distribution of the system's failure rate. Considering the difference between the posterior distribution of the failure rate and the probability distribution of the failure rate in the current test stage, the mixed probability distribution of the failure rate was constructed by introducing the similarity factor based on the KL divergence method, and then the integrated posterior distribution of failure rate was calculated by normalizing the mixed probability distribution of each failure rate. Based on the relationship between failure rate and reliability and MTBF, the probability distributions of the system's failure rate, reliability, and MTBF were established, and the Bayesian confidence limits of the system's reliability measures were estimated.

articleTitle: Research and Optimization of Frequency Measurement Algorithms Based on Monobit Receiver
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In the design of conventional single-bit receivers, a high error rate is often observed due to interpolation direction errors near the quantized frequency points caused by the Rife algorithm. To address this issue, this study proposes an optimization technique using a mean filter. By integrating this technique with single-bit quantization and approximate kernel fast Fourier transform (FFT), a 38.4Gbps ultra-wideband single-bit digital receiver based on a single-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and field-programmable gate array (FPGA) is designed. Subsequent MATLAB simulation and FPGA validation demonstrate that this receiver can reduce the frequency measurement error to within 3MHz, meeting the real-time or near real-time frequency measurement requirements for electronic warfare applications.

articleTitle: Fire Detection and Notification System in Real-Time Using a Lightweight YOLOv8-Based Detector
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In this paper, the FireDetection system is presented, which is designed to provide a robust and easily deployable solution for early fire detection. The system proposed uses the YOLOv8n detection model trained on an extended dataset, which includes detailed annotations for the presence of fire in each frame of the videos. The primary objective of this system is to furnish a resilient and readily deployable solution for early fire identification while simultaneously minimizing false positives and ensuring high frame rates to enable real-time applications. Through extensive experimentation, the results reveal significant enhancements in the model's performance, as evidenced by its analysis dataset accomplishments. With its robust architecture, advanced training, and reliable results, the FireDetection system emerges as a promising and valuable tool in the realm of fire prevention and early intervention, with potential applications in various scenarios that require swift and accurate fire detection. Finally, experimental results of this system demonstrate an improvement in state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: Flight Maneuver Recognition Through Modified YOLO Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Flight Maneuver Recognition (FMR) involves automatically recognizing patterns in air target maneuvers. Precise and real-time recognition of air target maneuvers from flight data is crucial for promptly analyzing and responding to the combat strategies employed by enemy air targets. Due to uncontrollable factors affecting the duration of flight maneuvers, the sampled data from the flight state parameters varies in length. Neural networks are extensively utilized in FMR due to the capacity of RNN's hidden states and CNNld's convolution kernel to handle input data with varying lengths. However, existing neural network models for FMR primarily concentrate on the classification task while neglecting the segmentation task related to flight data. This paper presents a modified YOLO-based multi-task learning neural network for FMR that enables neural networks to learn segmentation and classification tasks concurrently. Furthermore, an LSTM neural network was trained using the same simulated datasets, and comparative experiments show comparable performance in classifying flight data sampling points for both neural networks.

articleTitle: Blockchain Based System for Secure Production Information Management
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In the field of production, the collection, transmission, and storage of production information have a significant impact on production management. This paper proposes a blockchain-based secure production information storage and management system to address the issues of incomplete information collection, unreliable data transmission, and data isolation in traditional production information management systems. The system leverages the immutability and decentralization properties of blockchain technology to enable secure and efficient storage and transmission of the data. Moreover, a “step-hyperledger” structural mode is established for various business links in the pre-production, during-production, and post-production processes of safety production to achieve hierarchical management of data storage and full-process traceability. Combined with big data analysis techniques, the system facilitates effective pre-warning and efficient accountability after an incident. Simulation experiments and stress tests are conducted to validate the traceability interface of the system. The results indicate that the system demonstrates good stability even under the condition of multiple concurrent users, meeting the expected requirements and exhibiting certain advantages over traditional safety production systems.

articleTitle: MIFRL: A Model for Automatic Diagnosis of Laryngeal Diseases Based on Multi-Modal Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Insufficient clinical experience and heavy workload may lead to misdiagnosis or omission when manually analyzing laryngoscope images and diagnosing diseases. Based on deep learning, automatic diagnosis and generation of endoscopic reports are of great importance. Therefore, based on both text and image modalities, we propose the multimodal internal-related feature representation learning (MIFRL) network model for multi-attribute recognition and endoscopic reports generation. Firstly, text and image encoding modules are used to extract feature, which simplifies the process of manually labeling images. Next, internal-related feature mining module is designed for multimodal information fusion and class imbalance problem. Finally, a multi-branch structure is designed to output the multi-attribute recognition of the lesions and generate endoscopic reports. In addition, asymmetric loss (ASL) is introduced to further mitigate the class imbalance problem. Based on our dataset, the average accuracy of endoscopic reports and attributes classification were 85.5% and 90.7%, respectively. In the recognition of the smallest number of leukoplakia images, mean average precision (mAP) was improved from 81.4% to 86.7%. Compared with other models, our model also achieved better results.

articleTitle: Identification and Measurement of Sea Cucumber Based on YOLOv7 and GrabCut-RGBD
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The sea cucumber fishing ROV needs to select and grade the sea cucumber when it is fishing the sea cucumber. However, refraction and image quality seriously affect the recognition of sea cucumber by sea cucumber fishing ROV and the accurate measurement of sea cucumber size. This paper presents a new method of sea cucumber identification and size measurement based on YOLOv7 and GrabCut-RGBD. On the left eye correction image, the pretrained YOLOv7 sea cucumber detection model was used to identify the sea cucumber and locate the region of interest. A GrabCut-RGBD image segmentation method was used to segment two-dimensional sea cucumber objects on the region of interest, so as to obtain two-dimensional sea cucumber dimensions. The three-dimensional coordinates are obtained by triangulation, and the optimal size measurement point is found on the target image of sea cucumber to realize automatic size measurement of sea cucumber. The experimental results show that the accuracy of sea cucumber identification is 97%, and the average error of sea cucumber size measurement is 6%, which is better than the traditional method in sea cucumber identification and size measurement.

articleTitle: MRR-UNet: Skin Lesion Image Segmentation Based on Mixed Receptive Field Residual Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Medical image segmentation is a fundamental work in computer-aided medicine. The accuracy of segmentation results has an important impact on lesion-assisted analysis. Algorithms for segmentation of skin lesion image based on deep learning are significant for clinical diagnosis. However, these methods have the following challenges in extracting regions of interest: (1) The intra-class variability of different medical images is ignored. (2) Insufficient extraction of local information due to fixed-size convolutional kernel. In order to cope with these challenges, this paper presents a novel skin lesion image segmentation approach utilizing Mixed Receptive Field Residual Convolutional Neural Network as its foundation. In this paper, a Mixed Receptive Field Residual Module (MRRM) is designed to achieve better capture of multi-scale feature information. By utilizing Dilated Convolution and Depthwise Convolution with multiple sizes of convolution kernels, the proposed method achieves the capability to extract contextual semantic information within the field of view. And the residual structure enables better utilisation and reuse of low-level feature information. The proposed method achieves impressive results on ISIC2018 dataset, with an IoU metric of 83.42% and a Dice coefficient of 90.57%.

articleTitle: Detection of Ground Maneuvering Target Based on Range Frequency Reversal Transform and Searching Lv's Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: We present a solution to overcome the coherent accumulation problem for the ground maneuvering target, including range migrations (RMs) and Doppler frequency migrations (DFMs), based on the cascade of range frequency reversal transform (RFRT) and searching Lv's distribution (SLVD) technique. This novel long-time coherent accumulation method, synthetically referred to as RFRT-SLVD, has the capability to correct the third order range migration (TRM) and quadratic DFM (QDFM). In particular, RFRT is firstly implemented and can directly eliminate the RMs, according to the symmetric uniformly-spaced sampling of the range frequency, via multi-plying the echo data by its reversal data in range-frequency domain. Then, by constructing a phase compensation function, the QDFM can be removed. Finally, LVD achieves the signal energy accumulation. The major advantages of proposed method is that it accurately compensates the RMs and avoids the blind speed sidelobe (BSSL). In comparison with other representative algorithms, the RFRT-SLVD can satisfy both the detection ability and the computational complexity performance. Simulation data demonstrate the validity of the RFRT-SLVD method.

articleTitle: A Text Similarity Calculation Method with Feature Weighted Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Text similarity calculation is an important component of many text mining techniques. Most of the existing studies only consider model fusion of textual features or semantic features, which are not suitable for long text processing scenarios due to the time consumption of topic extraction for words of the whole document. This article introduces related work of text similarity calculation, including TF-IDF algorithm, lexical features and LDA(Latent Dirichlet Allocation) model. Then a text similarity calculation method that combines text word features and text implicit topic features is proposed, making full use of the surface and hidden information of text to calculate text similarity. The proposed method first improves traditional word mover's distance (WMD) algorithm by introducing lexical features of text, and then calculates text similarity by linear weighting of the improved WMD algorithm and LDA model algorithm. Experimental results indicate that compared with traditional WMD algorithm and LDA model algorithm, the proposed method obtains better text similarity calculation results.

articleTitle: Research on a Quantum Machine Learning Approach to Mismatched Filter Design
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In signal processing of radar systems, mismatched filter is required for suppression of sidelobes. In this work, we propose a quantum machine learning approach to generalized mismatched filter design, which is based on variational quantum algorithm architecture and is applicable to noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. The algorithm requires sufficiently less storage resources than its classical counterparts, and can be combined with other efficient quantum algorithms to provide building blocks for quantum signal processing workflows. The capabilities of the algorithm is analyzed with random waveforms and its bottleneck is also discussed in detail, with potential enhancement strategies put forward correspondingly,

articleTitle: A Method for Mining and Analyzing Time Series Patterns Related to Aerial Target
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: A method for mining and analyzing associated time series patterns of aerial targets is proposed to address the issues of high computational complexity and complex algorithm design under the condition of multiple elements of aerial targets. Firstly, preprocess the historical data of aerial targets and conduct preliminary screening based on a single element to reduce the data size. Then, by associating multiple elements, frequent subsequences are obtained and an associated dataset is established. Finally, mining the sequence patterns of aerial target association relationships based on rules. Through simulation experiments, this method can fully utilize the big data information of aerial target tracks and mine the activity patterns of targets in the time dimension.

articleTitle: Pulse-Related Distance Measurement Method
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Recently, Laser distance measurement technology has become much more developed, with the evolution of laser technology. Laser distance measuring equipment are also advancing in the direction of miniaturization, low power consumption and high accuracy. They are widely used in transportation, industry, military, aviation, aerospace and etc. In order to fulfill the requirement of miniaturization of laser distance measuring system, the energy of the emitted laser is inevitably reduced. To avoid influencing the measuring capability when using low-energy lasers, this research presented a pulse-related distance measurement method. It can effectively improve the measuring capability of micro-Joule laser with a low power consumption. Achieve the same effect on large targets (buildings, etc.) with the same effect as conventional high energy laser distance measuring equipment.

articleTitle: A Methodology for the Study of Frequency Response of the Active-Cascode Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology to study the frequency response of the active-cascode amplifier semi-quantitatively. It leverages on the sketching of asymptotic Bode plots to obtain the amplitudes and transition points of critical performance functions in the frequency domain. The plots provide helpful insights for guiding the process of manipulating device and system parameters to meet the ever-demanding design specifications, without complicated and sometimes intractable mathematical derivations. Reasonable accuracy of this methodology is justified by comparing the LTSpice simulation results with those obtained by this method, and considering the much less efforts involved herein. The usage of this methodology is also demonstrated by guiding the design process of frequency compensation.

articleTitle: Viterbi Soft Demodulation Algorithm for CPFSK Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Continuous Phase Frequency Shift Keying (CPFSK) is a phase-continuous constant-envelope modulation scheme. In modern communication systems, Turbo codes or LDPC codes are commonly used as error control codes to combat the effects of channel noise and fading. In the process of channel decoding, soft demodulation information is required to reduce the bit error rate(BER). This paper proposes a soft output calculation method for CPFSK signals based on the Viterbi demodulation algorithm. The method utilizes the difference of cumulative correlation values of the signal to characterize the log-likelihood ratio (LLR) information of the information symbols based on the derived results from conditional probability theory. These LLR values are then used as soft decision outputs. Simulation results demonstrate that, with almost no increase in algorithm complexity, this method achieves a performance improvement of approximately 3dB compared to hard decision demodulation.

articleTitle: Group Sparsity Based Higher Order Sparse Spectrum Fitting Approach for USV Localization
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The problem of unmanned surface vehicle (USV) localization is investigated in this paper. We develop a group sparsity based higher order sparse spectrum fitting (HOSpSF) approach to improve the accuracy of localization. In the proposed approach, the off-grid issue, and advantages of group sparse are combined. Firstly, a higher-order SPSF method is proposed to solve the off-grid DOA estimation problem by using the second-order Taylor approximation. Next, we present a USV localization approach that optimizes all sensor array nodes by incorporating the group sparsity theory. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method against the state-of-the-art arid-based approaches.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Imaging Technology of Cancer Lesion Area
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This research mainly involves the multidimensional imaging technology of tumor lesions removal, mainly using SALAM 3D algorithm, set graphics algorithm, multi-view geometric algorithm, convolutional neural algorithm, image edge classification algorithm, pattern recognition algorithm, interaction algorithm, stereo algorithm and vision algorithm. It achieves 2D to 3D through point cloud, graphics rendering quality update, Generative discriminative observation model, Transformer neural network architecture, Unreal 3D and other methods, and then uses point-based multimodal fusion method. In this study, the multi-arm mechanical principle is adopted to form a virtual lesion area through the point cloud, and the multidimensional imaging effect of the cancer lesion area is realized after the image rendering effect is adopted.

articleTitle: 3D Target Detection of Tractor in Agricultural Scene Based on Lidar
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Real time and accurate detection of agricultural machinery in the working scene is an important basis to improve the safety of agricultural machinery driverless and autonomous operation. This paper presents a 3D target detection method of tractor based on GNSS/INS/Lidar/camera data. Firstly, an on-board data acquisition platform based on multi-source sensors is constructed to obtain the tractor image, point cloud and position and attitude data of the acquisition vehicle in the common working scenes of agricultural machinery (machinery depot, tractor road and farmland), the data are time synchronized and space calibrated. Then, distortion correction of point cloud, the point cloud and image are jointly labelled, and the tractor test data set of images, point cloud and GNSS/IMU information is constructed. 643 frames of machinery depot scene data, 321 frames of tractor track scene data, and 320 frames of farmland scene data are obtained. The number of tractors selected is 6250. Finally, according to the characteristics of tractor driving and operation, the region of interest of tractor target detection is defined, the point cloud within its range is extracted, and the ground point cloud is filtered by RANSAC method. Then the data set is input into PVRCNN++ network for training according to the proportion of 5:1 between training set and test set, and finally the tractor 3D target detection model is obtained. The test results show that the detection accuracy of the model for tractors in machinery depot, tractor road and farmland are 90.21%, 87.59%, and 99.85% respectively, the recall rates are 86.72%, 95.13%, and 98.89% respectively, and the F1 scores are 88.43%, 91.20%, and 99.37% respectively. The model can better adapt to the agricultural scene.

articleTitle: A Link Prediction-Based Routing Maintenance Algorithm for Ad-Hoc Networks in Urban Rail Transit Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The application of wireless Ad-Hoc network technology in urban rail transit can improve the performance of urban rail transit vehicle-ground communication systems and is more conducive to meeting the demand of next-generation urban rail transit vehicle-ground communication. This paper focuses on the routing maintenance mechanism of urban rail transit Ad-Hoc network, and introduces a link prediction-based routing maintenance mechanism for the characteristics of trains moving at high speed in urban rail transit Ad-Hoc network, so as to avoid the problem of frequent link breakage when trains are moving forward, which leads to data transmission performance degradation. The relevant simulation results show that the proposed routing maintenance mechanism for Ad-Hoc networks of urban rail transit can provide more efficient data transmission methods while reducing the routing overhead in the network.

articleTitle: Greedy Sensor Scheduling with Energy Constraint
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a greedy algorithm to solve a sensor scheduling problem under energy constraints. Our goal is to reduce the total energy consumption, while maintain a predetermined threshold of estimation accuracy at each time slot. Meanwhile, the energy limitation of each sensor has to be satisfied. A greedy algorithm based on a truncate function is employed to tackle this problem. Furthermore, we adopt a group greedy strategy to enhance the performance of the proposed algorithm. The simulation experiments prove that the proposed strategy can effectively adress the problem and show superior performance.

articleTitle: Age for Relay Cooperative Energy Harvesting Networks with Finite Blocklength Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In this work, an earliest relay selection strategy is presented to minish the age of information (AoI) for finite blocklength transmission based energy harvesting IoT networks with multiple relays. Firstly, the decoding error rate is presented for both hops under selection combining scheme. Then, the statistical characteristics of the energy harvesting period and maximum transmission times are provided. Finally, the average AoI expression is derived and analyzed. Numerical experiment indicates that it can always identify the best packet length and selected relay number to minimize the average AoI.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for the Satellite Location Using Interferometer and Time Difference System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Compared with active localization, passive localization do not actively transmit any signals, has some advantages of low energy consumption, good concealment, and strong survivability. Two technologies, single satellite localization based on interferometer which is based on angle of arrival (AOA) and three-satellite localization based on time difference system, are widely used in scenarios of traditional space satellite passive reconnaissance and localization. Due to the long distance between the satellite and the ground, single satellite the reconnaissance and localization's accuracy is poor because of high signal propagation loss and constrained baseline length. However, the conditions for forming a three-satellite common view for time difference system are relatively strict, and a large number of emitter signals may only be received by single or double satellites at the same time. Therefore, we propose a new collaborative reconnaissance and localization method for interferometers and time difference systems (TDAOA). It is suitable for scenarios where a large number of emitter signals are only detected by binary satellites, and it does not require deblurring with high localization accuracy.

articleTitle: Fscope-IQA: A Novel Attention Design for Image Quality Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The existing algorithms for no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) always extract deeper features from low-level features, which often tend to the attention on salient objects. However, the purpose of IQA is not to evaluate the object-related regions merely but the entire image scope. Therefore, we design a full-scope attention guided image quality assessment algorithm (Fscope-IQA), in which there are three key elements: backbone, non-object attention features extraction module (NAFE) and cross-guided features coupling module (CGFC). We adopt the vision Transformer as our backbone. In the NAFE, the non-object attention features are acquired by the difference of the deep and shallow features. In the CGFC, a spatial mutual fusion is produced by exchanging and coupling distorted information between the object and non-object features. The full-scope information is obtained by repetitive combination of NAFE and CGFC, to compute the quality score in line with human vision. We performed experiments on both authentic and synthetic distortion datasets, and results show that our method could reach satisfactory performance over the up-to-date methods. The analysis illustrates that the full-scope attention is much more reasonable for NR-IQA than the object-oriented attention.

articleTitle: Subway Sliding Plug Door Fault Detection Based on Multiscale Sequence Entropy and Seagull Optimization-Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The subway sliding door system is an important part of the subway for ensuring the safe operation. To address the issues of high cost and low efficiency of the current subway sliding door fault detection methods, a fault diagnosis method based on motor current signal is proposed in this paper. The original motor current data are first preprocessed and segmented, then Multiscale Permutation Entropy (MPE) features are extracted from each segment. Fisher discriminant criterion is employed to further select the important features. Random forest model is utilized for fault detection, whose parameters are optimized by Seagull Optimization Algorithm (SOA). Experiments with real data have been conducted to test the proposed method. A remarkable prediction accuracy of 94% have been achieved in the results. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been verified.

articleTitle: Interpretability of Convolutional Neural Networks in Infrared Point Objects Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Deep learning has demonstrated remarkable advancements in the field of infrared point objects classification. However, the challenge lies in explaining the reasons behind their exceptional performance, which limits their application in high-reliability object recognition systems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a framework for interpreting convolutional neural network (CNN) models in the classification of infrared point objects. By leveraging the time sequence of infrared radiation (IR) emitted by point objects, we adopt the one-dimensional (1D) class activation map (CAM) technique to identify the positions within input subsequences that are relevant for classification. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method provides an explanation for how CNNs work in point objects classification. This not only enhances the reliability of CNN-based methods in point objects classification but also offers guidance for further improvement in model performance and interpretation of predictive results.

articleTitle: Parallel Light Source Based Machine Vision for Length Measurement of Shaft Part Chamfer
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Chamfering processing on shaft parts is an essential step for production and assembly. This paper studies the online chamfer length measurement of shaft parts by machine vision, aiming to establish an automatic machining quality ensuring system. The challenge of the measurement is that there is various interference on the cylindrical surface of shaft parts before final processing. If conventional imaging method is utilized, the interference may show visual characteristics similar to chamfer, leading to misjudgment. To solve this issue, we proposed a parallel light source based imaging method, which can illuminate the chamfer surface and suppress the reflected light from other areas. Additionally, a weighted least squares fitting based chamfer width calculation is presented to avoid the influence of iron filings and burrs. In experiments, the advantages of our technology in interference resisting are illustrated through comparison. The abnormal chamfer dimension on several shaft samples is successfully detected.

articleTitle: Multi-user Search on the Encrypted Network: a Lattice-based Proxy Re-encryption with Keyword Search
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Proxy re-encryption with keyword search (PRES) allows users to access encrypted data through different keys on the encrypted network. The function of PRES is the combination of public key encryption with keyword search (PEKS) and proxy re-encryption (PRE). PRES can be created by directly combining the two components, but this method is not practical since the resulting scheme is no longer proven secure. Moreover, most PRES schemes use classic security assumptions that are not able to address the issues of quantum computers. In this paper, we present a lattice-based PRES scheme. It is proven to be secure under the LWE hardness assumption.

articleTitle: Design of an Optical Receiver for Multi-core Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This paper presents an optical receiver designed to match multiple core optical fiber, implemented in a 0.18 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> CMOS process. The chip consists of a photodiode (PD) array and transimpedance (TIA) circuits, including the TIA core, Bandgap (BG) and Bias. The placement of PD array is highly matched with the multiple core optical fiber and each PD is followed by a TIA. The TIA achieves a 60 dB ohm transimpedance gain with a 200 MHz bandwidth and the input reference current noise is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.2 \text{pA} / \sqrt{ } \text{Hz}$</tex>. The BG can stably output a 1.2 V voltage and shows a good stability in the post simulation under 128 process corners. The Bias can provide the current required to drive TIA through a mirror transistor. Eye diagrams are shown when operating at bit rates of 200 M bps and 300 M bps with a forward input reference voltage of 1.2 V. While achieving high transmission efficiency, the chip area is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.78\times 0.92$</tex> mm2 which allows for more compact designs and suit for a wide range of application scenarios.

articleTitle: A Target Detection Method of Automotive Millimeter Wave Radar Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This paper introduces a research on automotive radar target detection using deep learning. Automotive radar faces the complex road environment, and the correct judgment of the location and attributes of the target around the vehicle is the key to safe driving. These works all use the Range-Doppler image data for detection. This paper finds four problems in traditional CFAR through experiments, and proposes a target detection method based on deep learning, which uses the YOLOv5 algorithm to better solve these problems.

articleTitle: Semantic Information Consistence Network: An Improvement Method for Cardiac Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease has a high death rate in the world. In recent years, automatic medical image segmentation methods based on artificial intelligence have been rapidly developed to facilitate the diagnosing of the disease. Unet, as a deep learning method, has been widely used in medical image segmentation for its stable segmentation performance. Due to the complexity and tiny morphology difference of pathological tissue, the performance of segmenting cardiac medical images by Unet is still not satisfactory. To improve the segmentation accuracy of cardiovascular images, a semantic information consistence network based on VIT-Unet is proposed in the paper. In the network, a multi-scale semantic compensation module is constructed to fuse semantic information of shallow and deep layers, and a feature-guided attention module is constructed to calculate the similarity of input features and fused features, and lead the expression of fused feature. The experiment result indicates that the network achieves better segmentation accuracy in cardiovascular images.

articleTitle: Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) Code Aided MIMO for Future Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This paper proposes maximum distance separable (MDS) code aided multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) framework, generally. The simulation results show that the schemes we propose can achieve better performance than quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) and spatial modulation (SM). There are two ways to generate MIMO framework based on MDS code: one is to combine MIMO with MDS code constructed by using amplitude and phase levels, called MIMO-MDS-APM framework; the other is to combine MIMO with MDS code, constructed by using in-phase and quadrature components of codewords, called MIMO-MDS-IQM framework. The proposed schemes are compared with QAM and SM schemes in terms of minimum Euclidean distance (MED). The results indicate that the MIMO framework based on MDS code can achieve better bit error rate (BER) performance under different detections, which can be seen as promising future wireless communication technology.

articleTitle: Time-Frequency Characteristics of Parachute Gun Shockwave Based on VMD-HT
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: During the ejection process of the fighter pilot, the parachute is shot out by the life-saving seat gun, which generates a shockwave that endangers human safety. In order to accurately and stably extract the time-frequency distribution characteristics, the shockwave signal is obtained through parachute gun shooting experiments, and features of the shockwave signal is extracted by using Variational mode decomposition and Hilbert transform methods (VMD-HT). VMD is a high sampling rate shockwave signal decomposition technique, which is suitable for analysing unsteady airborne parachute gun shooting shockwave signals. The HT method is used to accurately extract the relationship between time, instantaneous frequency and energy for the decomposed signal, and to obtain the marginal spectra. The analytic results show that the shockwave signal lasting 3ms has a significant energy concentration in the low frequency band of 0∽1kHz, which is important for the better protection of pilots.

articleTitle: Surrogate-Assisted Cooperative Lion Swarm Optimization Algorithm for High-Dimensional Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: With the development of information science, a large amount of data has poured into people's lives. As one of the effective means of extracting massive data, feature selection has been concerned by a large number of scholars. Feature selection is an NP-hard problem, and one of the traditional methods is to use optimization algorithms to search. However, this traditional method faces serious challenges with the increase of feature- dimensional data. This is mainly because as the feature dimension becomes larger, the search space of the optimization algorithm will increase exponentially, which will seriously degrade the search performance. Previous studies have shown that evolutionary algorithms assisted by surrogate models can solve high-dimensional feature selection well. Following this research line of thought, this paper proposes a surrogate-assisted cooperative lion swarm optimization algorithm for high- dimensional feature selection, which combines co-evolution and surrogate assistance with the lion swarm optimization algorithm to improve the accuracy of high-dimensional feature selection problems. Experiments show that the algorithm can show excellent performance in feature selection problems up to 6000 dimensions.

articleTitle: Research on Edge Cloud Storage Identity Authentication Mechanism Based on Multi-Layer Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Edge cloud storage is a novel data storage technology that utilizes the resources at the network edge to provide efficient and secure data services. However, there are multiple layers of identity authentication in edge cloud storage, which pose security risks. To address this problem, this paper proposes an edge cloud storage identity authentication mechanism based on multi-layer Integration that integrates the authentication of the terminal layer, transport layer, and application layer. The mechanism achieves the session binding of multi-layer authentication and improves the security and flexibility of authentication. It uses the edge cloud storage gateway as a proxy and establishes the mapping of authentication for each layer through the user authentication information directory. This paper analyzes and experiments with the proposed mechanism to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Parallel Combinatory Spread Spectrum System Based on Single Carrier Frequency Domain Equalization in Multipath Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: To solve the problem of performance limitation of direct sequence (DS) spread spectrum system in complex multipath environment, a parallel combinatory spread spectrum (PCSS) framework that combines single carrier frequency domain equalization (SCFDE) is proposed. Higher data rates and large processing gain can be achieved by PCSS transmission and the frequency-selective fading is overcome by frequency domain equalization, which is easy to implement at the receiver for the benefit of fast Fourier transform (FFT) and inverse fast Fourier transform (IFFT). Moreover, in order to balance the transmission rate and reliability in different environments and tasks, an improved PCSS framework with adaptive processing gain is investigated by deploying variable spread spectrum factors under the condition that the number of FFT/IFFT processing points is fixed, by which the control logic is very simple and it is convenient for real implementation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed PCSS schemes based on SCFDE show good performance in overcoming multipath fading. In the meanwhile, higher bandwidth utilization can be obtained compared with traditional DS strategy.

articleTitle: Attention-Based Noise-Aware Framework for Speech Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Speech enhancement performance of neural networks relies on the richness and completeness of training data, that show performance degradation for burst unseen noise. To solve this problem, we propose an attention-based noise-ware framework, that works feasibly with arbitrary single-channel speech enhancement model to enhance the realtime noise feature extraction ability of those models. Multi-head attention is applied to generate the predicted noise information by combining multidimensional noise bases derived from environment-related noise clusters in memory library. The predicted noise features are adaptively embedded at the input of traditional models to bring better robustness and awareness of unseen background noise. Mel-scale weighted loss function is proposed to combine the network training process with human auditory perception. Experiments prove that our framework outperforms baselines (LSTM and CRN) in both seen and unseen noisy scenes with various SNR.

articleTitle: An Improved FAST Corner Detection Algorithm for Real-Time Lane Lines Detection on Road Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Detecting near lane lines presents challenges due to the influence of large noise blocks on the road surface. This study proposes an improved algorithm for realtime lane lines detection to counter this problem. The algorithm is carried out in three key steps: First, a minimum filter technique is performed to remove salt noise within the image. Subsequently, a modified Features from Accelerated Segment Test (FAST) corner detection algorithm is utilized to further filter and eliminate the block noise. Finally, Sobel edge detection algorithm is employed to achieve precise edge detection results for the lane lines. The proposed method has been deployed on a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), with comparative tests illustrating both its feasibility and effectiveness in practical application.

articleTitle: Disentanglement of Speaker Identity for Accented Speech Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems have achieved good performance on standard English speech. However, recognition accuracy significantly degrades for non-native speakers with accented speech. Existing multi-accent ASR models utilize accent embeddings as extra input to handle diverse accents, but these embeddings often intertwine other speech attributes, impeding model performance. In this paper, we propose a speaker identity disentangled accent modeling approach, which extracts the accent embedding without any speaker-specific information, and uses it to improve the performance of the multi-accent speech recognition systems. Experiments conducted on the CommonVoice dataset demonstrate that our proposed method attains a 15% reduction in word error rate (WER) over baselines.

articleTitle: Random Forest Distance Estimator Based on Monocular Egocentric RGB Camera in Human-Robot Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This paper presents a method for obtaining 3D gesture poses from monocular RGB camera images. A random forest based distance estimator is constructed and trained to generate depth information for hands. Furthermore, to improve efficiency, we employ a federated learning approach to reduce the model complexity of random forests. The RNN recognizes the topological structure of the hand, transmitting two-dimensional information of the hand keypoints to a random forest for the corresponding distance estimation. Experimental and application demonstration results show that this method can obtain stable 3D gestures from 2D images and reduce the complexity of the system implementation and registration. Because of input normalization, it can adapt to other cameras without the need for preconfiguration. Therefore, this method offers an effective and cost-efficient solution for obtaining 3D gesture poses, resulting in a significant cost advantage in the application of human-robot collaboration and making it highly promising for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Dehazing Algorithm for UAV Image Based on Smooth Dilated Convolution
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are widely used for tasks such as remote sensing mapping, ground target detection, and environmental information extraction. Their advantages lie in the broad aerial perspective, versatile shooting angles, and suitability for different scenarios. In regions characterized by frequent rain and fog, the presence of significant moisture significantly affects the image quality of UAV aerial imagery. This results in reduced contrast, changes in tonality, and obscured details, severely limiting the ability to derive meaningful information from these images. Traditional deep learning-based image-dehazing algorithms rely too much on atmospheric scattering models and are prone to color distortion and detail loss. The end-to-end image-dehazing algorithm presented in this paper uses a smooth dilation convolution approach. Unlike conventional methods based on the atmospheric scattering model, this technique achieves a direct end-to-end dehazing process, seamlessly transforming the input image into a clear output. The color distortion phenomenon can be effectively solved through experiments.

articleTitle: Lossless Compression for Hyperspectral Images Using Cascaded Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In the paper, a three-level cascaded prediction based lossless compression method for hyperspectral imagery (HSI) is proposed. This method contains three main steps: preprocessing, prediction and coding. Firstly, k-means algorithm is employed to classify spectral vectors in preprocessing stage. In the prediction stage, a three-level cascaded predictor consisting of a similar neighborhood mean (SNM) predictor, a low-order recursive least squares (RLS) predictor and a high-order least mean square (LMS) predictor is adopted. SNM predictor is used to eliminate spatial redundancy, RLS predictor is used to eliminate spectral redundancy, and LMS predictor is used to obtain final predicted value. Finally, Huffman encoder is employed to encode the prediction residuals. The experimental results demonstrate that this method combines the advantages of the three predictors, significantly reduces the computational complexity and improves the compression effect.

articleTitle: Weakly-Supervised Temporal Action Localization Based on Attention Regularization
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The primary objective of temporal action localization is to identify the beginning and end moments of actions in unedited videos. We propose a weakly supervised temporal action localization model based on attentional regularity to address the difficulty of accurately identifying these temporal boundaries. Weakly supervised action localization frequently encounters the issue of conflating actions and backgrounds as a result of the absence of frame-level labels. To address the problem of difficulty in distinguishing actions from backgrounds, we introduce an attention mechanism to improve the loss function, which after attentional regularization allows the model to more accurately distinguish between actions and backgrounds. We construct a pseudo-label mutual supervision mechanism to achieve more complete localization supervision in order to reduce potential omissions during action localization. Extensive tests on benchmark datasets like THUMOS14 show that our method outperforms other weakly supervised methods in terms of average accuracy.

articleTitle: Outage Performance Analysis of Full-Duplex Cooperative Nonorthogonal Multiple Access System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This paper investigates the outage performance analysis for a downlink cooperative nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) network over Nakagami-m fading channels. Specifically, the strong NOMA user exploits full-duplex (FD) mode, while the decoded forwarding relay strategy is employed to improve the outage performance in terms of the weak user. We first derive the closed-form expressions of outage probability for both legitimate users and the considered system. To achieve a more comprehensive analysis, the FD-based self-interference is also taken into account. Then, Monte Carlo simulations have been presented to verify the accuracy of the theoretical derivations. Finally, the analytical and numerical results manifest that the proposed scheme outperforms the benchmark scheme. Also, the outage performance can be further enhanced through proper power allocation optimization.

articleTitle: Binary QC-LDPC Codes Based on Whiteman's Generalized Cyclotomy
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This study introduces a construction method for QC-LDPC codes, ensuring their absence of four-cycles by utilizing Whiteman's generalized cyclotomic (GC) classes. An analysis of the cycle structure within the Tanner graph for the proposed codes, specifically focusing on cycles with length six, is conducted. Moreover, this paper presents the necessary and sufficient conditions for generating GC-QC-LDPC codes with a minimum girth of eight, based on the analysis. Simulation results demonstrate the superior bit error rate (BER) performance of the constructed QC-LDPC codes over the AWGN channel. Compared to other QC-LDPC codes, QC-LDPC codes constructed using this method have a reduced base matrix size for long code lengths. This attribute augments their suitability for integration within storage systems.

articleTitle: Soldier Behavior Analysis with AR-Based Machine Vision and Big Data Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: To recognize the soldier behaviors according to the videos or images with Big Data analysis and Augmented Reality (AR) devices, the images was processed with intelligent techniques, and then used as the training samples and testing samples with deep learning neural network. In order to extend the intelligent application to the network, the deep learning model was encoded into JavaScript model, and could be utilized as a web application version via browser, WeChat and APP. The ResNet model was improved with the TensorFlow model, and the system framework of soldier behavior analysis was optimized with the PSO algorithm. In the experiments, the noises of the soldier images were filtered with the Laplasse high-pass filter. The behaviors of single soldier from the single-soldier image and multiple soldiers from the multiple-soldiers image were recognized with the core functions of the TensorFlow model and the skeleton models. Experimental results show that this intelligent approach is novel and useful to analyze the soldier behavior with the samples form the network. Furthermore, the web model could be optimized and fasten to improve the performance of this approach.

articleTitle: User Behavior Prediction Based on Oil Consumption Data
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Accurate prediction of user behavior has important application value in various fields. By understanding and predicting user behavior, businesses can make informed decisions and optimize their marketing strategies. In order to be able to accurately predict user purchase behavior, we propose a new user behavior prediction method. Firstly, the user consumption amount and consumption times are preprocessed, secondly, we use random forest (RF) for feature screening, and use long short-term memory network (LSTM) to construct a user behavior prediction model. Finally, we use the sparrow search algorithm(SSA) to optimize the hyperparameters of the model. Experimental results show that our RF-SSA-LSTM model can make accurate predictions of user behavior.

articleTitle: Rocky Desertification Feature Extraction and Spatio-temporal Evolution Analysis based on Decision Tree
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Karst rocky desertification is a kind of land degradation phenomenon which is harmful and difficult to control. Rocky desertification monitoring based on remote sensing technology is an effective method. In this paper, Chongzuo and Qianxinan Prefecture in Guangxi Province are used as experimental areas, Landsat8 TM / OLI remote sensing images and ASTER GDEM elevation data are used as data sources, and three factors of vegetation coverage, bedrock exposure and slope are used as characteristic variables. The decision tree is constructed to extract the information of rocky desertification in the study area, and the rocky desertification grade is divided according to the experimental results. Finally, the temporal and spatial evolution characteristics are analyzed and discussed. The results show that: 1.
