The area of rocky desertification extracted in this paper is 94.5 % consistent with the land survey data. 2.the area without rocky desertification in Chongzuo increased by 11.25 % from 2010 to 2020; the area without rocky desertification in southwestern Guizhou increased by 8.36 % and the area of severe and extremely severe rocky desertification decreased by 10.31 % and 5.58 %, respectively. 3. The methods and conclusions of this paper can provide methods and data support for the evaluation of ecological security and rocky desertification control.

articleTitle: Bangla Speech-based Emotion Detection using a Hybrid CNN-Transformer Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Robots are now widely employed in various scenarios to interact with humans. It is vital that the robots understand the speaker's emotion and respond accordingly. Humans possess innate abilities to recognize emotions from speech, but it is challenging to provide machines with the same capabilities to predict emotions from human speech. Recently machine learning and deep learning techniques are employed for emotion recognition tasks. Due to emotions such as angry, surprise etc. being predominant for only few time frames of an example audio of that class, it becomes difficult to detect them and models often have a hard time for these classes. We employ a hybrid CNN-Transformer approach where we attempt to solve this problem by having both locally receptive convolutional features and globally receptive attention features contributing to final classification. We evaluate our approach along with other standard approaches in BanglaSER dataset. We report weighted class accuracy of 92.3% using our proposed approach achieving significant performance gain over current literature.

articleTitle: A Method for Evaluating the Status of Converter Valves Based on Siam-LSTM Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: As the key equipment of DC project, the converter valve bears electrical and thermal stress for a long time, and the real-time mastering of its operation status is the key to the safety and stability of DC project. In this paper, a converter valve state evaluation method has been proposed by constructing a converter valve state evaluation model based on Siamese network combined with long and short term memory network (LSTM), using Siam-net grid structure to train LSTM network parameters, effectively relying on a small amount of sample data to complete the extraction of converter valve state features, and considering the temporal characteristics of sample data, using LSTM network to complete the evaluation of converter valve state. Using PSCAD to build a simulation model of the converter valve, we experimentally prove the effectiveness of the state evaluation method and realize the accurate assessment of its operating status, which is of engineering guidance to ensure the stable and safe operation of the converter valve equipment.

articleTitle: Generalized Enhanced Convolution Block for Super-Resolution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Balancing the computational complexity and performance of CNN-based super-resolution (SR) networks is a challenging task in practical scenarios. Leveraging linear reparameterization techniques to improve model performance with minimal negative impact is a promising approach. In this work, we find that previously proposed re-parameterization techniques do not adapt well to different architectures of SR networks or yield significant performance gains. Hence, we propose a highly versatile and high-performance re-parameterization block called Generalized Enhanced Convolution Block (GECB) for efficient training of SR networks. During the training phase, GECB can replace grouped k × k convolutions with N groups for efficient training. GECB has six different paths with carefully designed structures, aimed at improving the representation capability of various features and generating more adaptive gradient updates. During the inference phase, GECB can be transformed to a normal convolution, without affecting the original model structure. Additionally, we further investigate the gradient update rules of GECB to demonstrate its outstanding adaptability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our GECB achieves similar or better performance than previous SR re-parameterization methods on multiple benchmark datasets. Moreover, our method can adapt to a broader range of network architectures, making it applicable to more SR networks and enhance their performance.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation of OFDM System Based on BR-SRGAN Network
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In the existing channel estimation methods of OFDM systems, a naive deep learning-based algorithm cannot fulfill the expected fidelity and high-frequency details are varnished at higher resolutions. A Generative Adversarial Network algorithm based on super resolution techniques and bilinear residual is proposed in this paper, to estimate traditional channel through the image processing. Firstly, the training dataset is generated by the Physical Downlink Shared Channel of the 5G New Radio standard. Then, converting the generated channel matrix of the pilot frequency position to a low-resolution image. And, utilizing neural network model to substitute the channel estimation interpolation processing. The MSE of our method is able to consistently reach 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup>, indicating that the algorithm we proposed has outstanding performance and prominent robustness than the traditional algorithms, such as LS, Practical Channel Estimation, ChannelNet and ReEsNet network.

articleTitle: Graph Contrastive Learning and Auxiliary Intent Across Sessions for Session-Based Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The target of session-based recommendation is to predict the future behaviour of the user based on limited amount of data over a short period of time in the past, which faces two key challenges: severe data sparsity, and dynamic user intent. A new kind of Contrastive Learning approach is presented in this research that is effective for the session-based recommendation task. Our method involves an effective data augmentation technique, which adds noise to the embedding space in a uniform manner to generate two contrastive views. We then apply Contrastive Learning to supervise these views, preserving complete session information and maintaining efficient graph augmentation to solve the data sparsity. Moreover, in order to better infer the dynamic intention of the current user, we exploit the intent of similar users in a subtle way. It is experimentally demonstrated that our approach outperforms the SOTA session-based recommendation methods in three real-world datasets.

articleTitle: LprViT:An Efficient ViT for LiDAR-Based Place Recognition Using Range Image
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Place recognition is a crucial component in the realm of simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) and autonomous driving. It can also enhance the performance of loop closure detection and global localization. LiDAR-based place recognition usually relies on global feature descriptors to accurately express the similarity between LiDAR scans. However, it is time-consuming to extract and generate the global feature descriptors from the original LiDAR data. As a result, treating LiDAR-based point clouds place recognition as a 2D image problem using range projection is becoming an increasingly common and successful strategy. Vision Transformer (ViT) is a Transformer model based on self-attention mechanism for image classification. Through self-attention mechanism, ViT out-performs CNN at modeling the global information of images. We investigate that whether ViT can be transferred to LiDAR-based place recognition tasks. Firstly, we introduce a new convolutional stem to replace the original linear embedding layer in ViT. Secondly, we establish synergy by integrating low-level fine-grained features from new convolution layer with high-level coarse-grained features from ViT by skip connections. Thirdly, we aggregate these features to construct the global feature descriptor via the NetVLAD technique. The results of experiments on KITTI confirm that our method can operate online and achieve superior performance on par with existing approaches.

articleTitle: Research on Explosive Identification and Localization for Explosive Filling Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: At present, in the domain of blasting engineering, the predominant approach for filling explosives involves manual labor. To facilitate the smooth grasping of explosives by the robot, a visual detection algorithm is proposed. This algorithm is designed to identify and locate explosives, enabling the robot to replace the manual process of loading explosives in demolition blasting scenes, an experimental platform for explosive identification is built to simulate the demolition blasting environment, and machine vision and YOLOv5 neural network are used to identify and locate explosives. Firstly, based on YOLOv5 convolution neural network, the identification experiment of explosives under different environmental factors is carried out, and the location of explosives is located based on the principle of binocular vision measurement. Finally, the pose and size of explosives images processed by image morphology are detected. The depth and pose information of explosives in three-dimensional space are obtained to provide the information needed for explosive loading robot to successfully grasp explosives. The experimental results show that only when the camera is within 800mm from the explosive, the shielding degree of the explosive should not exceed 50%, and the dust concentration is lower than 100g/m3, can the position and attitude in the explosive space be accurately detected.

articleTitle: A Modified Multivariate Variational Mode Decomposition for Multi-channel Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The multivariate variational mode decomposition (MVMD) is an optimization-based method that allows simultaneous processing of non-stationary multi-channel signals. It has recently garnered considerable attention due to its excellent signal separation capability and robustness against the sampling frequency. Nevertheless, MVMD also encounters certain challenges. Specifically, in cases where the signal is significantly disturbed by noise, MVMD struggles to accurately decompose the correct sub-signals. Moreover, the computational time required for MVMD increases dramatically with the number of channels, thereby making it challenging to solve multivariate signals with high-density channel. An effective solution to these issues is the implementation of the proposed modified MVMD (MMVMD) technique. This method aims to convert the task of finding multiple multivariate oscillations corresponding to MVMD into finding multiple univariate oscillations in one-dimensional space. The satisfactory noise robustness and faster decomposition rate of MMVMD, especially for signals with a large number of channels, are demonstrated by its application on multivariate synthetic signals. We finally provide further convincing validation of the effectiveness of the algorithm through the analysis of a 4-channel EEG signal.

articleTitle: A Data Security Exchange and Sharing System Construction Method and Perfomance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Sensitive data faces security risks of theft, tampering, or abuse during the exchange and sharing process. This paper proposes a new method for constructing a data security exchange and sharing system based on the above risks, and improves attribute-based access control technology to achieve policy conflict resolution through dynamic authentication and multi-party joint authorization. On this basis, real-time recording technology based on Merkle tree is used to achieve tamper proof forensics and precise traceability of data. The experimental results show that the data security exchange and sharing system has the advantages of high encryption speed as well as search efficiency, and has the characteristics of supporting multi-party joint authorization and short response time for access control.

articleTitle: Efficient Resource Allocation Scheme for Aperiodic Traffic in NR V2X Communications Through Adaptive Reservation and Selection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: New Radio Vehicle-to-Everything(NR V2X) Mode 2 communication of the 3rd Generation Partnership Project(3GPP) has focused on the distributed resource allocation technique for the aperiodic traffic. However, due to the unpredictable generation intervals of the aperiodic traffic, it is challenging to predict accurately the random arrival moment as done in the periodic traffic, resulting in ineffective resource allocation when using the traditional Sensing-Based Semi-Persistent Scheduling (SB-SPS) scheme. Besides, the state-of-art reservation techniques with a changeable Resource Reservation Interval (RRI) seem not sufficient to handle intensive impacts of both selection collision and extra collision-induced delay between vehicular UEs during an aperiodic traffic transmission. In order to meet the low-latency and high-reliable QoS requirements of aperiodic traffic traffic in NR V2X Mode 2 communication, it is worthwhile in this paper to propose a novel effective resource allocation scheme namely ARSAP through the adaptive Reselection Counter (RC) and RRI adjustment, which is optimized by the joint critical value detection on both packet collision ratio and collision-induced persistent delay. Furthermore, a novel adaptive resource reservation technique with a matched RRI set related to RC and RRI adjustment can be designed to effectively accommodate the resource allocation for the upcoming aperiodic traffic. In addition, both the theoretical derivation of the performance metric and the simulated evaluation results are also given. It can be seen that the new proposed algorithm can achieve superior communication qualities such as high Packet Reception Ratio(PRR) and low delay to the counterparts, even in the highly-dense vehicular networks.

articleTitle: Unknown Forgery Method Recognition: Beyond Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: N owadays, deep learning-based generative models are capable of producing high-quality spoofed speech. This presents new challenges for audio forensics, such as detecting spoofed speech and understanding how it is created. Current work is either limited to true-or-false detection or classification, or simply groups all samples from forgery classes unseen during training to an unknown class. In this paper, beyond classifying all samples from unseen classes as unknown, and considering the correlations between different classes, a cluster analysis-based embedding extractor training method is proposed to learn representations of speech forgery methods, which has good generalization ability to unknown speech forgery classes. In this method, a merged speech forgery recognition dataset is firstly constructed with more categories and more speech samples based on manually created labels. Based on this dataset, an embedding extractor is trained by finetuning a pre-trained Transformer. Subsequently, clustering is conducted with the embedding representations to label each sample as a cluster index. The pre-trained transformer with the same network structure is again finetuned on the new dataset with the cluster indexes as labels. The finetuned transformer acts as the final embedding extractor. Finally, the extractor is used to obtain the embedding representations and predict the number of classes of unknown data based on clustering analysis. Extensive experiments are performed on publicly available datasets. From the experimental results, the following two conclusions can be drawn: (1) Embedding extractors trained on clustering-based merged datasets have a better ability on traceability generalization to unknown forgery methods compared to embedding extractors trained on label-based merged datasets. (2) As the number of forgery method classes in the training set increases, the trained embedding extractor has better traceability generalization to unknown forgery methods.

articleTitle: A Pulse Position Demodulation Method for Underwater Optoacoustic Communication Based on Cepstrum-Wavelet Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The optoacoustic pulses generated under the thermal expansion mechanism have good repeatability and high correlation coefficient, making them suitable as carriers for underwater communication. However, due to the unique properties of optoacoustic signals and the limitations of laser physical parameters, the pulse position modulation (PPM) is the only feasible modulation scheme at present. This paper proposes a pulse position demodulation method based on cepstrum-wavelet decomposition, which can achieve the separation of noise and optoacoustic pulses in the cepstrum domain, and complete comparative judgment by calculating entropy value. Finally, simulation results confirm that the performance of the cepstrum domain demodulation method is superior to traditional methods, and the feasibility has been verified through experiments at Zhoushan Pier.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Memory Protection Mechanism Adhering to the Specifications of AUTOSAR OS SC3
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: As the dynamics of intelligentization, connectivity, electrification, and collaborative processes within the automotive sector persist in their rapid evolution, there has been an escalating focus on the matter of functional safety within vehicular operating systems. Within the context of this evolving landscape, the present scholarly work offers an exposition on the conception and realization of a memory protection mechanism in adherence to the AUTOSAR OS SC3 standard. In response to the limitations inherent in traditional memory protection mechanisms, necessitating manual configuration of address ranges for the determination of protection intervals, this novel mechanism introduces an approach for the dynamic acquisition of addresses and the establishment of protection range parameters. The practical execution and empirical assessment of this mechanism transpired on the Infineon AURIX TC275 microcontroller. The outcomes of the testing procedures elucidate that this approach not only fulfills the requisites of memory protection but also augments code portability and development efficiency.

articleTitle: Over-the-RIS Modulation: A Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Assisted Modulation Design
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved over the air modulation (OTAM) scheme by using the powerful reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs), namely over-the-RIS modulation (ORM). In the design framework, we reconstruct multipath channels by employing several RISs to increase the attenuation difference between multiple paths. Compared with conventional OTAM, ORM can be used in more generic fading scenarios, e.g., channels with non-ideal attenuation properties, and thus extends the application of OTAM. Based on the Bayesian criterion, we propose an optimal likelihood detector for the ORM system and derive a closed-form expression of the bit error rate (BER). Furthermore, we investigate the phase optimization of the RISs to improve its BER and deduce its closed-form solutions. Simulation results are presented to show that the proposed ORM system can achieve a better BER performance and higher transmission rate than the conventional OTAM systems, especially for environments with severe shadow fading.

articleTitle: Application of MSCT Post-Processing Technology in Forensic Identification of Rib Fractures
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The presence or absence of rib fractures and the number of fractures are important criteria for forensic identification of human injuries. The clear diagnosis of each rib fracture is directly related to the identification of disability level and compensation amount, as well as the determination of the nature of violent cases. In forensic forensic expertise, it is required to clarify whether rib fractures occur and the specific number of roots and locations, while identifying new and old fractures to avoid misdiagnosis and missed diagnosis and ensure judicial fairness. This study takes 163 cases of rib fracture identification accepted by our unit from 2018 to 2022 as samples, adopts MSCT and its post-processing technology for retrospective research, and analyzes the application of MSCT post-processing technology in forensic rib fracture identification, especially in the identification of concealed, incomplete and old rib fractures. This study used two post-processing CT scans for pre and post comparison to diagnose acute traumatic rib fractures, with an accuracy rate of up to 100%. After 21 to 30 days of trauma, the formation of bone callus reached a very obvious state. During this period, CT examination is not only beneficial for displaying occult fractures, but also for excluding fractures caused by short-term re trauma. It can be used as the best time for forensic appraisal. Through this study and literature review, it is necessary to fully utilize the advantages of different post-processing techniques in identification, select appropriate post-processing techniques, clarify the relationship between injury and disease, exclude old fractures, identify hidden fractures, and avoid misjudgment.

articleTitle: Action Perception Machine for Gait Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Gait recognition is one of the most promising video-based biometric techniques. Gait is a periodic movement comprising sequential actions that involve different body parts. Therefore, in a gait cycle, complex structural changes in pedestrian silhouettes contain rich temporal semantic information. However, the existing gait recognition methods based on silhouette sequences are significantly insufficient in temporal semantic representation. This study designs an Action Perception Machine (APM) with a temporal attention mechanism to fully utilize temporal gait information and extract salient action features. First, APM adaptively fuse context information of different time scales to perceive diverse actions. Then, the APM realizes cross-time interaction between actions to capture the salient moments. The two folds enable the APM to have strong temporal semantic representation ability for motion sequences. We integrate the APM into a part-based gait recognition framework (APMGait) to extract discriminative fine-grained gait features. Extensive experiments on the CASIA-B, GREW and Gait3D datasets revealed that the APMGait with a simple network outperforms state of the art.

articleTitle: A Transferred Graph Laplacian Regularization Approach for Color Image Denoising
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Image denoising is an ill-posed problem because noise interference during image acquisition frequently leads to serious image degradation. To mitigate this problem, we present a different definition of the normalized graph Laplacian matrix, which consists of a kernel similarity matrix and a related dual random symmetric matrix. Furthermore, we provide the transferred graph Laplacian regularization (TGLR) approach under the manifold structure, which assumes the smoothness of the graph frequencies on the data manifold and promotes the non-local self-similarity property that natural images exhibit. Specifically, the transferred graph Laplacian implicitly encapsulates the graph Fourier basis that interprets image denoising as a graph filtering problem based on data-adaptive Laplacian filters. Finally, an improved steepest descent (SD) algorithm is employed to solve effectively the presented color image denoising problem with symmetry and positive definiteness. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms several state-of-the-art denoising methods in the objective and subjective qualities.

articleTitle: Fire and Smoke Detection Method Based on Improved YOLOv5s
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Fire always threatens human life and property safety, causing huge economic losses and casualties. This paper introduces an enhanced version of the YOLOv5s model, which focuses on fire and smoke detection. The main goal is to overcome the shortcomings of conventional fire detection systems, particularly slow detection times and a high number of false alarms. The proposed algorithm aims to improve the efficiency and accuracy of fire and smoke detection by leveraging improvements made to the YOLOv5s model. The improvements include integrating the CA (Channel Attention) mechanism module and the Transformer module into the feature extraction part, effectively reducing feature redundancy without sacrificing information. As a result, the algorithm achieves more accurate flame and smoke detection. The experimental results demonstrate that the enhanced fire and smoke detection model achieves a significant improvement in mean average precision (mAP) compared to the original YOLOv5s model. Specifically, the mAP of the improved model is 14% higher, indicating a substantial enhancement in its ability to accurately detect fire and smoke instances.Additionally, the size of the improved model is only 14.4MB, and it achieves a detection speed of 68 frames per second. This signifies that the improved model not only enhances detection accuracy but also meets the requirements of real-time and lightweight fire detection simultaneously.

articleTitle: Iterative Achievable Rate Adaptive Beam Alignment for THz Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Beam alignment is a key technology to ensure reliable initial access and data transmission in THz communication systems. This paper proposes an iterative achievable rate adaptive beam alignment method which iteratively searches for the optimal codebook layers of initial training and termination training based on the achievable rate criterion. Besides, in beam training at each codebook layer, the pilot sequence length of each training codeword is adaptively adjusted based on the preset detection probability as well as false alarm probability, which significantly improves the success rate of beam alignment. In order to demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method, comparative simulations were performed. The results show that a higher success rate has been achieved in the proposed method compared with the exist methods although the pilot cost was slightly reduced, resulting in more reliable access and higher transmission rate for the systems.

articleTitle: Open Set Recognition of Radar Signals Based on Time-Frequency Fusion and OVA Network
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: For open electromagnetic environment, most of the radar signal modulation recognition methods available cannot handle the open set recognition well. To overcome this problem, a time frequency fusion and One-vs-All (OVA) network based radar signal open set recognition algorithm is proposed. Firstly, combining the advantages of Wigner-Ville distribution (WVD) with high time-frequency resolution and Choi Williams distribution (CWD) with a good cross terms suppression ability, a multi time-frequency image feature fusion algorithm based on wavelet transform is proposed, where fusion criteria for low-frequency and high-frequency components of the image are designed to improve the quality of time-frequency images. Then, a radar signal open set recognition method based on OVA network is proposed, where a closed set classifier is used for pre-classification, and the OVA network is trained with the most similar negative samples to maximize the classification boundary of similar categories, and its classification confidence is improved via open set entropy minimization strategy and threshold judgment. For closed set scenario simulations, it can achieve 92.6% accuracy with signal to noise ratio (SNR) of -6 dB and have the ability to handle small sample cases. What's more, for open set scenarios, both known and unknown modulation types of radar signals can be recognized well.

articleTitle: Neural Network for Odor Sensor Array Spike Encoding Inspired by Mammalian Olfaction
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Signal processing in electronic nose (e-nose) odor detection involves a series of complex and time-consuming steps, such as noise reduction, filtering, normalization in signal preprocessing, as well as feature generation, selection, and dimensionality reduction. When dealing with different gas sensors, these processing methods might require meticulous adjustments, and each sensor might need own specific processing strategy. Such strategies are often tedious and overly reliant on intricate feature engineering, leading to time-consuming operations and poor reproducibility. To address this issue, this paper proposes a biomimetic olfactory perception model inspired by the mammalian olfactory system. Unlike traditional e-nose methods, our model deeply simulates the core structures and functions of the mammalian olfactory system, especially the biomimetic design for neural conduction and information encoding. This allows the model to directly handle the raw sensor responses of the e-nose, eliminating the conventional preprocessing and feature selection steps. The experimental results show that our biomimetic model achieved an average recognition rate of 95.8% on a traditional Chinese medicine dataset, significantly outperforming the traditional method's 90.84%. The model not only demonstrates excellent feature extraction capabilities but also shows extreme robustness when the types and numbers of sensors change, enhancing the reliability and accuracy of the electronic nose in practical applications.

articleTitle: A Marine Environment Simulation Model for Cross-media Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The cross-media communication network is important in the fields of marine resource exploration, search and rescue, cross-domain unmanned combat system and so on. The ocean buoy can function as a communication relay in the cross-media communication network. Traditional terrestrial network topologies or protocols may no longer be applicable in the sea due to the marine environment. The current network simulation platform does not support simulation in the marine scene, thus a network model of the marine environment is proposed to analyze the effects of the marine environment in this paper. In order to simulate the influence of wave fluctuation on wireless transmission between buoys, a buoy motion model with the variation of buoy antenna height and inclination with waves is proposed. At the same time, a radio propagation loss model with two-ray reflection loss and water vapor absorption loss is added in the network model. Both are modeled in the NS-3 network simulation platform. Based on this simulation platform, the throughput performance of the two routing protocols DSDV and DSR under sea states 1, 3, 5, and 8 is verified. The results show that the network throughput shows a gradual downward trend with the increase of sea state level, demonstrating the applicability of the suggested marine environment simulation model. Furthermore, the simulation results show that DSR has better performance than DSDV in low to medium sea states.

articleTitle: Research on Acquisition Method of DSSS System Based on PMF-FFT
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Spread spectrum communication, as an essential communication technique, has a wide range of applications in the real world. This article focuses on the acquisition methods in DSSS (direct sequence spread spectrum) systems. The PMF-FFT (Partial Match Filtering Fast Fourier Transform) algorithm, recognized as an excellent acquisition algorithm, combines timedomain and frequency-domain acquisition algorithms, exhibiting characteristics such as high dynamic range and fast acquisition speed. Firstly, the basic principles of the PMF - FFT algorithm are introduced, and a corresponding mathematical model is established to analyze the characteristics of this algorithm. Secondly, improvements are made in response to the practical design requirements and issues in multi-rate, multi-user communication systems. These improvements mainly include the selection of spread spectrum sequences, frame composition, and acquisition architecture. Through these improvements, the algorithm's performance is enhanced. Finally, through simulation verification at rates of 16Kbps and 128Kbps, the improved algorithm successfully achieved acquisition of eight different time slots under a significant Doppler frequency.

articleTitle: The Automatic Tongue Image Analysis Algorithms in Traditional Chinese Medicine Diagnosis and Treatment
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Tongue image analysis, a key method in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), is widely used in clinical practice. This study aims to develop and validate a computer-assisted algorithm for tongue image analysis to improve diagnostic accuracy and consistency. A diverse range of tongue images was collected from patients of different ages, genders, and health conditions. We applied image processing and machine learning techniques to automatically categorize tongue characteristics, including tongue color, shape, texture, coating quality, and coating color. These characteristics were then compared with clinical diagnostic results. Extensive validation experiments demonstrated precision rates of 90%, 80%, 89%, 90%, and 91%. Furthermore, we conducted research to establish connections between these tongue characteristics and specific health conditions. This research highlights the algorithm's effectiveness and efficiency in tongue image analysis and its relevance in associating tongue characteristics with medical conditions.

articleTitle: MedSyn: Medical Image Synthesis of Brain Magnetic Resonance Images Based on Hybrid Information Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is widely used in clinical scenarios. However, acquisition of certain image modalities may be in limitation due to multiple considerations such as time duration and labor costs. Hence, medical image synthesis can resolve those limitations by estimating the desired target image modality without inducing an actual scan. In this paper, we proposed a novel method which aggregated the hybrid information of MRI to improve the performance of medical image synthesis and addressed it as MedSyn. Specifically, the MedSyn adopted the GAN framework, and made some great improvement. In generator, we proposed a simple yet efficient Tri-Focus Visual Center (TVC) to activate contextual features by establishing inter-dimensional dependencies with the assistance of rotation operations and gaussian functions. Furthermore, we proposed a Hybrid Global-Local Feature Extractor (HGL) module to capture long-range dependencies and exploit potential relationships between spatial and channel dimensions to extract global-local information. Benefitting from the modules of TVC and HGL jointly, the generator could capture obvious image features and underlying semantic information. In discriminator, we proposed a Dynamic Multi-Scale (DMS) Discriminator which could enhance discriminative ability by combining features of different scales dynamically. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, we conducted experiments on three brain datasets (the Meningioma dataset, the IXI dataset and BRATS dataset), and compared the results with some state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results showed that our MedSyn outperformed other state-of-the-art methods in terms of both quantitative evaluation and qualitative visual assessments.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection Model for Data Interactions Based on Temporal Features in Electric Power Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The current power data centers face the risk of data leakage during the data exchange process. Given the increasing scale and complexity of power data centers, traditional methods for identifying anomalies in the temporal characteristics of data interactions are not applicable. However, there is currently no specific model available for identifying abnormal data interaction behavior in the context of power data centers. Directly using existing models would result in low efficiency and fail to meet the requirements of power data center systems. This article proposes a model, VAE-GAN, for identifying abnormal data interaction behavior with multivariate temporal characteristics specifically designed for power data center business scenarios. The Variational Auto Encoder (VAE) architecture allows the model to learn in an unsupervised manner. The use of Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) and their architecture helps address the drawbacks of VAE networks in terms of smoothness and reconstruction ability in latent spaces, thereby improving the model's generation and reconstruction performance. Experiments were conducted on a dataset provided by a power company to study the effectiveness of the VAE-GAN method in power data center business scenarios. The results demonstrate its usability in the context of power data centers.

articleTitle: SS-MAF: Semi-Supervised Echocardiographic Segmentation Using Multi-Atlas Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Left ventricle (LV) segmentation in echocardiography is of paramount significance in cardiac function analysis. Recently, semi-supervised segmentation has garnered considerable attention due to its potential mitigation of labeling costs. Despite this, most semi-supervised methodologies tend to overlook the specialized anatomical priors specific to echocardiography, often yielding suboptimal outcomes. Simultaneously, atlas priors have been validated on other organs and imaging modalities. However, their direct application in echocardiography is fraught with challenges, primarily attributed to the indistinct boundaries of the LV and the presence of fan-shaped image edges, which impede atlas image registration. This paper presents a new method of semi-supervised segmentation using multi-atlas fusion, named SS- MAF, which is designed to incorporate atlas priors tailored for echocardiography while circumventing the intricate image registration process in traditional atlas-based methods. The SS-MAF comprises two components: a Multi-Task Learning (MTL) module and a Multi-Atlas Fusion (MAF) module. The MTL module serves precise landmark localization and segmentation estimation. The MAF module is primarily focused on the generation of probabilistic atlases, utilizing annotated atlas data with the guidance of key landmarks to facilitate the automatic annotation of unlabeled data, avoiding the traditional image-level registration, thus enhancing the performance of the MTL module. Our SS- MAF is rigorously evaluated on the publicly available CAMUS dataset, with results demonstrating its superiority over other state-of-the-art semi-supervised segmentation techniques in echocardiography.

articleTitle: Recursive Deconvolution Algorithm Based on Least Mean Square Error
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: This paper presents a recursive deconvolution algorithm to address the problem of low computing efficiency in previous deconvolution algorithms. This study implements a recursive algorithm that may decompose the deconvolution process into signal sampling time intervals based on the matrix inverse lemma. This approach runs in parallel with the signal sampling process, lowering computing complexity and enhancing the efficiency of deconvolution computation while also laying the theoretical groundwork for real-time deconvolution computation. Next, the algorithm can be applied to the deconvolution solution of unknown signals with fixed-length variables and variant-length variables. Furthermore, this approach decomposes its computational complexity into each recursive link, which makes it possible for high-complexity deconvolution calculation to be applied on low-end chips. Finally, the computational complexity of the proposed method is analyzed theoretically, and the simu-lation results illustrate the calculation error and noise immunity performance of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Indoor Positioning Based on the Integration of IMU and UWB
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Accurate indoor location information is of utmost importance for the navigation of modern indoor mobile robots. However, achieving accurate positioning solely with ultra-wideband (UWB) technology in indoor environments is challenging due to the susceptibility of UWB measurements to non-line-of-sight (NLOS) effects. To address this issue, this paper proposes an indoor positioning system that integrates an inertial measurement unit (IMU) with UWB. Firstly, an analysis of the errors present in UWB measurement data leads to the development of a two-step calibration method based on least squares (LS) to estimate error parameters. Subsequently, an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF)-based integration localization algorithm for IMU and UWB is proposed to mitigate the impact of NLOS. Through comprehensive simulations, the suggested algorithm's performance is assessed and contrasted with the weighted least squares (WLS) approach. Experimental findings show that the two-step LS-based calibration method estimates error parameters with accuracy. Moreover, the EKF-based IMU and UWB integration algorithm achieves approximately half improvement in localization accuracy compared to WLS, it also demonstrates excellent robustness. Consequently, the suggested indoor positioning system, which integrates IMU and UWB, satisfies the requirements for accuracy for indoor mobile robot navigation.

articleTitle: A Virtual Surgery System for Lung Biopsy
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: An advanced preoperative rehearsal system for lung puncture biopsy surgery is designed to address the issue of the high operator requirements and high risk of postoperative complications. The system enables the creation of three-dimensional model of both the lung and the puncture needle. It mechanically models the skin, fat and muscle of the chest wall to establish a virtual surgical rehearsal environment combined with force feedback technology. The realism and ease of operation of the system were validated based on analyzing various parameters from simulated lung puncture surgery performed by 20 volunteers. The results indicate that the system has high degree of effectiveness and clinical value that can serve as an auxiliary tool in lung puncture surgery.

articleTitle: A Joint Multi-Gradient Algorithm for Demosaicing Bayer Images
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: In image sensors such as CMOS and CCD, de-mosaicing is usually required to replace Bayer-format images with RGB-format images. Poor de-mosaicing algorithms can produce zipper effects and pseudo-colors, etc. In view of this situation and the hardware requirements of image devices, the original de-mosaicing technology gradually fails to meet the practical needs. On the other hand, although the deep learning-based de-mosaicing technology is more effective, the computational volume is too large, occupies too much hardware resources, and is difficult to be realized on the hardware platform. Therefore, this paper proposes a de-mosaicing algorithm based on multi-gradient union, which improves the traditional gradient-based first-order differentiation method, designs a new gradient operator, and ultimately judges the image edges by means of four gradient direction decisions to interpolate along the image edges. Experiments show that the algorithm in this paper has better recovery in image edges as well as texture complex regions with higher PSNR and SSIM values and better subjective visual perception compared to the traditional gradient algorithms such as BI, Cok, Hibbard, Laroche, Hamiton, while the algorithm involves only the add-subtract and shift operations, which is suitable to be implemented on the hardware platform.

articleTitle: High-Capacity Reversible Data Hiding in Encrypted Images Based on MSB Bit-Plane Serpentine Rearrangement and Compression
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Reversible data hiding techniques in encrypted images (RDH-EI) have been extensively researched to safeguard the privacy of images. To enhance the embedding capability of RDH-EI algorithms and security, this work leverages the topological coherence within the input plaintext image to create more additional space for embedding confidential information prior to image encryption. Initially, the prediction error of the input image is computed using the pixel prediction technique. Subsequently, the bit-plane serpentine rearrangement mechanism and the bit-stream compression method are employed to further enhance the process. This compression technique efficiently compresses the most significant bit-planes, resulting in a high-capacity space for embedding. Finally, the end-user successfully extracts the data and restores the input image using the possessed keys. The results clearly show that the proposed approach achieves not only attains a superior embedding capacity which achieves the maximum average embedding rate with a value of 3.624 (bpp), but also obtains a commendable reconstructed image quality that is PSNR=+∞ and SSIM=1.

articleTitle: FORM: Finding the Fair-Optimal Ridesharing Matching on Road Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: Fairness in ridesharing attracts much attention from academia and industry in recent years. One of the typical definitions of fairness among passengers comes from the stable matching problem. Some studies employing this concept apply existing Basic Roommates Algorithm (BRA) to randomly yield a fair matching or fail to find one. In this paper, we aim to find the optimal fair matching that satisfied by the most passengers. Specifically, we propose the fair-optimal ridesharing matching (FORM) problem, and prove its np-hardness by the reduction from optimal roommates problem. To tackle FORM, we propose two methods, namely Worst Passenger Selection (WPS) and Minimum Cost Selection (MCS), based on the key operation of BRA. We prove the approximation ratio of WPS is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{4}{7}$</tex>. Besides, we devise GFRM method to handle unsolvable case to guarantee a fair solution. Finally, we extend our solution framework to a more general scenario where more than two passengers sharing a ride together. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate the efficiency and effectiveness of our proposed approaches on New York City taxi trip data set. In summary, our framework improves the total cost saving of passengers by 9% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 15\%$</tex> (compared with BRA) and the platform revenue by 17% (compared with the state-of-the-art passenger matching algorithm GAS) with a guarantee of the fairness among passengers.

articleTitle: Research on the Regulation Strategy of False Propaganda of Live E-commerce Based on Three-party Evolutionary Game
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The problem of false propaganda in live e-commerce is becoming increasingly prominent and serious. Based on this background, the article constructs a game model between the main stakeholders of false propaganda in live e-commerce, i.e., live-streaming platforms, live e-commerce sellers, and government regulators, from the perspective of evolutionary games, and uses MATLAB to simulate the behavior of stakeholders. It is found that: at the early stage of market regulation, government regulators do not need to strengthen regulation, and at the middle and late stage of regulation, increasing the intensity of regulation will prompt live e-commerce sellers to develop regulated behavior fully. The fine system is bounded. When the number of fines set by government regulators meets the condition of making the live e-commerce sellers' choice of false advertising strategy less profitable, it is meaningless to increase the amount of fine regulation strategy. Improving the detection rate of false propaganda violations by live broadcast platforms is a key strategy in the regulation of false propaganda for live e-commerce.

articleTitle: Harmonic Extraction of the Joint Synchronous Extrusion Wavelet Transform and Triangular Basis Function Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Communication, Image and Signal Processing (CCISP)
abstract: The parameter identification of time-varying harmonic signals has an important application value. For the frequency of harmonic signals, the synchronous squeezed wavelet transform (SWT) can be used to identify them more accurately, but due to the effect of modal aliasing in the decomposition process, the SWT has a large error in identifying the amplitude and phase values of time-varying harmonics. In order to reduce the recognition error of SWT in harmonic amplitude and phase values and further improve the recognition accuracy, this paper proposes a new method of parameter recognition by combining SWT and triangular basis function neural network. Firstly, the time-varying harmonics are decomposed by SWT, the number of harmonic components is calculated according to the decomposition results, and the estimated value of the frequency of each harmonic component is preliminarily recognized based on the coefficients of SWT decomposition. Then, on the basis of the preliminary recognized values of frequencies, the triangular basis function neural network framework is constructed, and the frequencies, amplitudes and phases of the harmonics are used as the weights of the network, and the learning is carried out in the network by an iterative method. Finally, the network is trained by using the most rapid descent method, and according to the weights of the network after convergence, the frequency, amplitude and phase of the harmonics are converted respectively to realize the accurate identification of the harmonic parameters. The effect of the proposed method is verified through experiments, and the experimental results show that the method in this paper can recognize the frequency, amplitude and phase of harmonics with high accuracy, and when the harmonic signals are contaminated by strong noise, the method in this paper can also accurately recognize the harmonic parameters, and the recognition accuracy is much better than the classical SWT method.
